# SPD-055 — Bash hook: an assignment-shaped word after a wrapper is its command, which the hook skips as an assignment (Law 7)

## Brief
After strip_wrapper the prefix loop reads the wrapper's arguments as shell words, so NAME=value is taken for an assignment and dropped; the wrapper (nice, command, exec, nohup, timeout, xargs ...) execs that word, and a word holding a slash runs as a path.

Evidence: Probed from the SPD-043 scratchpad (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2, sh) with a directory named 'x=.' holding a fake git: nice x=./git push ran git push in all four; the hook reads push as the command, kind other, no finding. env and sudo do take NAME=value as environment, so the fix is per wrapper. SPD-043 left wrapper arguments as before; only the shell's own command position stopped reading expanded words as assignments.

## Size, persona and model decision
Cluster B of Eric's batch of 2026-09-15, with SPD-062 and SPD-051, second engineer on opus.
